text:
Priya (PM): Quick note from the offsite — we need a tighter prioritization rubric for multi-region + multi-tenant isolation work. can we sync on what 'launch-ready' actually means for this bigpile?
Diego (Eng): +1. customers keep asking for predictable p99 and clear residency guarantees. we should avoid vague promises.
Lena (Infra): Agree. propose a Launch Readiness Matrix: telemetry, perf SLOs, capacity model, chaos-tested failover, and operator runbooks.
Marcus (Arch): +1. also add a routing policy catalogue (known-compatible fallbacks) and a migration path for tenants. don't want ad-hoc per-customer exceptions.
Sasha (Eng-ML): Adding quality gating: baseline evals on representative prompt sets, and a regression budget (e.g. max 1% drop in top-n Rouge/BLEU-ish metric or prompt-level accept rate) before we let traffic route.
Olivia (CS): Customer ask: enterprise legal wants documented data residency and an SLA for cross-region failover. Pilot customers will need a test window.
Priya (PM): Drafting a decision canvas for the rubric. sketch so far: 1) Safety & data residency: signed KVs + audit logs; 2) Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets per region; 3) Capacity economics: committed vs burst; 4) Operational playbooks.
Diego (Eng): For Latency SLOs we should define test harnesses. sample: synthetic tail tests with sequence_lengths = [64, 512], load profile = 0.1->1.0 QPS, and KV-cache cold/hot cases.
Lena (Infra): Also include an "evacuation" acceptance test: simulate region loss and assert < 2x latency and < 5% error spike within 3 minutes.
Marcus (Arch): How about a policy taxonomy doc that maps customer tiers to guardrails? e.g., Tier A = dedicated pools + strict affinity, Tier B = regional affinity + soft fallbacks.
Sasha (Eng-ML): We should standardize the model variant fallback rules: prefer same quantization class, same tokenizer, and max logits-shift threshold to avoid hallucination regressions. put it in the policy catalogue.
Olivia (CS): On the cutover side, customers will want canaries and an opt-in switch. plan: 1 day canary at 5% traffic, automated rollback on metric triggers.
Priya (PM): Decision needed: do we treat multi-tenant isolation as a single epic or split into three milestones? my recommendation: Milestone A = Guardrails + Routing DSL, Milestone B = Telemetry + SLOs + Eval harness, Milestone C = Tenant migration tooling + dedicated capacity workflows.
Diego (Eng): Splitting helps parallel workstreams. we'll need a small infra spike for the routing DSL first. Marcus and Lena: can you own the DSL design doc?
Marcus (Arch): Happy to. will include examples for: preference, hard-affinity, quarantine, and cost-prioritized fallback.
Lena (Infra): I'll outline the infra reqs (network egress, KMS, audit) and the evacuation playbook. estimate 4 sprints for infra core.
Sasha (Eng-ML): We'll build the eval harness and a sample prompt set repo. need product to provide customer personas and 3 canonical datasets.
Olivia (CS): I'll collect ask lists from three pilot customers (FinTech, HealthTech, and Marketplace); will push them into the template by EOD Thu.
Priya (PM): Great. let's define measurable launch criteria now so engineering can plan. proposed concrete gates: 
- Telemetry: per-route retention + traces enabled and dashboards published.
- Performance: p99 <= 250ms for short seq (64) and <= 1200ms for long seq (512) under normal load for Tier A pilot.
- Reliability: cross-region failover exercised in staging with automated rollback verified.
- Quality: eval regression <= 1% on curated prompt sets; human spot-check rate <= 5% for canary.
- Economics: end-to-end per-token cost delta <= 1.5x of baseline for Tier A (with docs explaining tradeoffs).
Diego (Eng): Those look actionable. can we add an "operational readiness" metric: runbook pages with playbook steps and oncall run-through checklist completed?
Priya (PM): Added. also need sign-off matrix: Arch, Infra, Eng-ML, Security, CS, Legal. all must sign to move from B -> C.
Marcus (Arch): Suggestion: include a migration staging environment where we rehearse tenant cutovers at scale (10 tenants with production-like traffic) before actual customer cutovers.
Lena (Infra): We'll provision a sandbox fleet for that, but needs budget approval. rough cost estimate: 2–3 dedicated nodes for 4 weeks.
Olivia (CS): I'll coordinate pilot timing and customer windows. clients prefer low-traffic windows (weekends).
Sasha (Eng-ML): For the eval gating, propose a small automation: canary run outputs a CSV of metric deltas and a pass/fail flag based on thresholds. that enables CI gating.
Diego (Eng): Nice. ops question: where do we keep policy versions? need an immutable policy registry so we can trace which routing policy shipped with which model version.
Marcus (Arch): Plan: policy registry + immutable hashes stored in audit log (KMS-signed). will sketch API for lookups.
Priya (PM): Action items: Diego+Sasha: draft test harness and canary automation prototype (due in 2 weeks). Marcus+Lena: initial DSL spec + infra acceptance tests (due in 2 weeks). Olivia: customer templates and pilot windows (due EOD Thu). I'll draft the Launch Readiness Matrix and share.
Olivia (CS): noted.
oncall-bot: Reminder: #product weekly sync in 1 hour.
Diego (Eng): quick Q — should we include quantization compatibility in the DSL? seems important for fallback decisions.
Sasha (Eng-ML): yes, tag variants with "quant_class" and prefer same class or fall back only if eval pass. add to DSL.
Priya (PM): Final ask: let's keep this thread as the single source for the offsite action-list. I'll push the matrix doc in 48 hours and request review. :raised_hands:
Marcus (Arch): ack.
Lena (Infra): ack.
Sasha (Eng-ML): ack.
Olivia (CS): ack.
Diego (Eng): ack.
